#330. Head of AI Native Operations at Supabase

Supabase is the Postgres development platform, built by developers for developers. We provide a complete backend solution including Database, Auth, Storage, Edge Functions, Realtime, and Vector Search. All services are deeply integrated and designed for growth.

We are looking for a Head of AI Operations to own how Supabase works.

Supabase is building an AI-native internal operating system: a common way of working across the company where AI carries a meaningful share of the operational load rather than sitting alongside it as an assistant. We are standing up a new central team to build those systems, enable the teams, and embed AI operations throughout the organization. This is the role that runs it.

You will own the maturity model teams are assessed against, the standards that define how work happens here, and the operating cadence, under one design rule: every recurring meeting has to justify why an automated report cannot replace it. You will lead a small team of senior individual contributors, one building the platform and one running enablement.

The premise is that process encoded as agents scales where process enforced by people does not. Your job is to prove that is a repeatable pattern rather than an anomaly, across teams you have no authority over.

We are fully remote and async. The document is the enforcement mechanism here, which means the standards themselves are your deliverable.

Own the maturity model end to end: The rubric, the scoring method, the evidence standard, and the appeals path. Every team ends up with a published assessment and a written plan to its next level.

Run assessments and commitments: Conduct assessments with department heads yourself, landing them as commitments with named owners and dates rather than opinions.

Own the standards layer: Define how work gets tracked, decisions get proposed and resolved, teams migrate onto shared tooling, and stale documentation gets retired. Standards ship as documents teams follow without being chased.

Fix the decision process: Ensure written proposals reach resolution instead of accumulating unresolved by defining stages, exit criteria, and closing mechanisms.

Run the operating cadence: Lead automated weekly reporting, a regular blockers-and-decisions forum, a monthly leadership review, and a quarterly board-level format. Delete meetings a report could replace.

Manage rollouts: Execute private assessments first so leads see only their own and have time to move, followed by a pre-committed public transparency date.

Wire standards into onboarding: Ensure every cohort arrives pre-trained rather than inheriting nearby habits.

Build and direct the team: Hire, grow, review, and direct two senior individual contributors (platform and enablement) without doing their work for them.

Measure and publish outcomes: Measure and publish whether the thesis holds by tracking how much coordination work agents absorb versus what a human program office would cost.

Every standard you write should be the input to something that enforces it, and every enforcement mechanism should produce the evidence that grades it. When you write the rule that work must carry a current status, you are not finished until a report finds the stale items and tells their owners without you in the loop. The same applies to your own function: the team you build gets assessed by the model you own, published next to everyone else's, and you should want that.

The default outcome for a company-wide standard is that teams politely ignore it. So the first question about any standard is not "is this correct" but "what will make people route around this," and the design follows from that answer. Same for meetings: rather than asking what a new sync would accomplish, ask what report would make it unnecessary and build the report. Same for the public transparency date: it gets committed before anyone has a score to defend, because afterwards the lobbying is rational.

You direct agents rather than doing the work by hand, and you can tell whether the direction was any good. That means reading an agent workflow definition and knowing the procedure is too broad, reading a data model and challenging the metric behind it, reading a pull request from your own team and sending it back. Your working artifacts are files in version control that agents can read, not chat transcripts. You will not build the platform. You will be the person who says whether what got built is right.

Scale & Cadence Experience: Have run operating cadence and program discipline at a company crossing ~200 to 800 people while remote and async.

Agentic AI Expertise: Have personally built agentic AI workflows that others depended on. You can read/review an agent workflow definition, a data model, and a pull request to judge quality.

Standard Adoption Track Record: Have taken a standard from zero to company-wide without direct authority over adopters, with a clear mechanism that made it stick.

Async Communication Skills: Are an exceptional writer who leverages documents as enforcement mechanisms.

Accountability: Are comfortable being graded publicly by the system you build alongside every other team.

Have run a maturity model or capability assessment across teams you did not own, published results, and driven organizational reallocations.

Are native to Git, Markdown, and Pull Requests (whether through engineering or technical operations background).

Have permanently eliminated a recurring meeting by replacing it with an automated system.

Deep software engineering background is a plus, but not required.

Standards land without chasing: Rules are written, published, wired into onboarding, and followed because non-compliance is automatically visible.

Universal coverage: Every team has an evidence-backed assessment, owner, and written path to the next level, with disagreements handled through published appeal channels.

Firm transparency dates: Assessments transition from private to public on pre-committed dates without exception.

Net-negative meeting time: By year end, the operating rhythm consumes less calendar time across the organization than when you arrived.

Autonomous operational function: Your two reports operate independently against written charters, at least one non-reference team runs a genuinely automated production workflow, and you focus on review rather than execution.

We hire globally. We believe you can do your best work from anywhere. There are no Supabase offices, but we provide a WeWork membership or co-working allowance you can use anywhere in the world.

We operate asynchronously and trust you to manage your own time. You know what needs to be done and when.

We look for positive team players who are self-driven and results oriented, with excellent attention to detail. The best candidates show that they are forward planners, reliable and determined, and keen to assume responsibility for projects, processes and policy. If you like to take responsibility and you like to ensure that things are done properly and efficiently then you will enjoy the role tremendously.

Location: This is a global operation, we have open roles in teams in all time zones.

We revisit compensation annually (and more often for graduates and associates) to ensure we recognise outstanding performance. In addition to base pay, we offer a performance-driven annual bonus. We provide all team members with additional benefits, which reflect our values and ideals. We balance our programs to meet local needs and ensure fairness globally.

We recruit on a global basis and set a very high standard for people joining the company. We expect excellence - in order to succeed, we need to be the best at what we do.

#335. Staff Product Manager, AI Agents at Clutch

Clutch is building a portfolio of AI agents for credit unions — collections (Emma, already sold and live with multiple credit unions), plus new agents in origination, fraud, engagement, and activation. This role owns one of those agents end to end: discovery with members and credit union executives, the first implementations, and the roadmap that follows.

This is not a traditional product management role. You will spend a large share of your time in front of customers — often on site — shaping products that don’t fully exist yet, then staying with them through the first implementations until they actually work in production. The next year is deliberately an experimentation year: listening, prototyping, and learning what credit unions will really adopt.

You will also help decide where each agent lands. Our largest partners will eventually run several agents, each with a different internal owner (a VP of Collections buys very differently than a VP of Lending). Part of the job is judging which agent goes live with which credit union, in what sequence, in collaboration with the other AI PMs — rather than pushing your own agent into every account.

You’ll join a small, senior AI product group inside Clutch that operates like a seed stage startup within the company, working shoulder to shoulder with a dedicated AI engineering team and a growing bench of AI engineers.

The team is unusually close to the commercial side. You’ll have a commercial counterpart with more influence on your roadmap than a PM is typically used to, because the way we land and expand these agents is still being invented. You’ll also work alongside AI Ops Managers, who take an agent to scale once it is defined and live with the first one or two customers.

It is a high-ownership, low-process environment: strongly opinionated people, fast decisions, and a lot of ambiguity that you are expected to resolve rather than escalate.

Ramp on the agent portfolio and on the credit unions that matter most over the next six months

Rapidly prototype and live trial different agents and use cases.

Take ownership of one agent and its roadmap, and build a working relationship with your engineering and commercial counterparts

Join customer conversations and go to atleast 2 on-site visits, and start forming your own view of the customer and the product

Meet the internal buyers’ counterparts at our largest partners and understand who owns what inside a credit union

Own discovery for your agent: run customer sessions on site, and turn what you hear into a sequenced roadmap with clear business outcomes. Goal is to ship an agent every 4-6 weeks in production

Ship the first version of the integrations your agent depends on (core, loan origination system, CRM), designed to be reused rather than rebuilt per customer

Drive at least one net-new product go-live, making key decisions and clarifications that unblock it

Work with the other AI PMs to decide which credit unions your agent should launch with, and which should wait

Have your agent live with multiple credit unions, with data you can show partners to prove it is working

Expand the business outcomes your agent is accountable for, beyond the initial use case

Hand scaled rollout to AI Ops with documentation and a repeatable integration pattern, while you keep the product roadmap

Be trusted to walk into a partner executive conversation alongside commercial counterparts and come out with a decision

Product sense above all. You have strong product judgement, taste and customer intuition

B2B product experience. You have directly managed enterprise customers, negotiated scope, and pushed implementations to completion.

AI-forward. You have built something with AI yourself and can demo it. Deep AI research experience is welcome but not required; curiosity plus shipped work is

Customer presence. You can run a room with a credit union’s leadership team, on your own, and sell a direction before the product exists

Willingness to travel. Expect roughly 20% on average, with stretches of 50% during critical windows. Being on site measurably increases how fast we close customers with direct product coverage and how fast we launch

Relentless forward motion. You need to be persuasive and comfortable pushing without authority

Top-notch communication, written and live. Fast, clear, high-quality customer responses

7+ years in product management in a fast-paced environment, preferably in B2B SaaS and/or Fintech, Founding backgrounds are strongly welcome

Nice to have: financial services or fintech background; experience in or alongside a forward-deployed engineering or product function; hands-on integration work with core banking, LOS, or CRM systems

Remote Flexibility: Enjoy the freedom of remote work from anywhere, balancing life and career seamlessly.

Unforgettable Off-Sites: Twice a year, bond with colleagues in exciting destinations, fostering teamwork and fresh ideas.

Paid Time Off: Enjoy flexible PTO days yearly for relaxation and rejuvenation.

Stock Options: Joining us means having a stake in our success, so you'll receive stock options as part of your compensation package.

Home Office Setup: Create your ideal workspace with a dedicated budget for home office essentials.

Work Trip Budget: Grow personally and professionally with a budget for work-related trips and co-working.

Health Coverage: Prioritize your well-being with comprehensive health and dental insurance plans.

Clutch is a revolutionary vertical SaaS company, proudly backed by Andreessen Horowitz (A16z), aimed at revolutionizing the way Credit Unions engage and change the lives of their members. As a champion of financial well-being, we address the urgent need for affordable lending solutions in an era where the average American grapples with over $155,000 in household debt.  Unlike traditional financial institutions, Clutch develops software to turn Credit Unions into FinTech lenders and leverage their balance sheets to responsibly lend to over 130M Americans. Our mission extends beyond mere financial transactions; we strive to fundamentally enhance the way credit unions interact with their members. By integrating cutting-edge technologies and user-centric designs, we help credit unions provide seamless digital experiences that are on par with leading tech companies. This approach not only preserves but revitalizes the longstanding tradition of community and member-focused service inherent to credit unions.

#337. Forward Deployed Engineer at Clutch

Clutch builds AI agents that work on behalf of credit unions. Emma, our collections agent, is live at five credit unions and handled 60,000+ member conversations in her first twelve weeks at one of them. Behind her is a growing portfolio: origination, fraud step-up, member (re)engagement and activation agents, all built on the same Agents Platform (TypeScript, NestJS, our own agent SDK, MCP, Temporal, promptfoo).

As a Forward Deployed Engineer you are one of the two engineers on an agent. You take it from "sold" to "live and performing" at a specific credit union: you sit in the discovery sessions, you build the integrations to their core banking and loan systems, you author and tune the agent's behavior, you run the live tests with their staff, and you stay with it through go-live and the first weeks of production. When something needs a person in the room, you are the one who flies. You are based in the US and can be at a credit union in the Midwest or the Southeast within a day or two, not a week.

This is a senior engineering role, not a solutions or support role. You write production code in our monorepo every week: integrations, modules, and the agents themselves (prompts, tools, evals), together with the other engineers on the pod. The difference from a traditional engineer is that you are on site more often, you make judgment calls in front of the customer, and you own the outcome. What you learn in the field flows straight back into the product: defaults, playbooks, and the platform capabilities the next agent will need.

You build; our AI Operations Managers deliver. The pod (pod lead plus engineers) designs and builds each agent in a high-touch way with the first customers. Once the agent is defined and live, AI Ops coordinates the implementations, configuration and ongoing success at the next credit unions. You hand them something that works and a playbook to run it.

You'll join the Agents team, a small, senior group operating as a startup inside Clutch: seven engineers, a dedicated AI product group, and AI sales specialists, working directly with some of the largest credit unions in the country. Every agent is staffed by a pair of engineers, one leaning toward the conversation and LLM side, one toward software and integrations, with a pod lead who owns the product day to day. There is no layer between you and the customer, and no layer between you and the platform team.

The operating style is direct, written, and evidence-driven: BLUF updates, evals over opinions, business outcomes over ticket counts. The team is spread across Brazil, Argentina and the US and works async by default. Being on site is a tool we use at specific moments (kickoff, live testing, go-live), not a permanent posting.

Ship your first production change to a live agent through the team's review process, and be able to explain how a member's call flows through the Agents Platform end to end

Learn one agent deeply: system prompt, tool contracts, orchestration triggers, compliance gates, and the implementation process from kickoff to go-live

Join at least one credit union implementation as the second engineer, including a live testing session with their staff

Map where the current implementation process loses time and where a default or a tool would have removed a round trip

Own the technical side of one credit union implementation end to end: core and LOS integration, agent configuration, testing, go-live, and the first weeks of production

Run the eval and tuning loop for your agent (golden transcripts, rubric judges, regression suite) and be trusted to change its behavior without a second engineer checking your work

Have completed at least two on-site visits and turned what you heard there into product decisions with your pod lead and PM

Contribute at least one reusable capability back to the Agents Platform that the next implementation will not have to rebuild

Have taken one net-new agent from sold to live at its first credit union, with data you can show the partner

Be the engineer credit union staff ask for by name when something in their deployment needs to change

Have written the implementation playbook for your agent well enough that the AI Ops team runs the second and third credit union without you

Be shaping what the next agents look like, because you have seen where the current ones break in the field

In rough priority order. Prior LLM or ML experience is not required. We can ramp the agent skills; we cannot ramp senior engineering judgment.

5+ years of software engineering in a fast-paced environment, preferably in SaaS and/or Fintech, with senior TypeScript and Node.js backend experience in a large codebase (NestJS, CQRS, schema-validated boundaries, dependency injection). We do not count years of AI experience; the field is too young for that to mean anything. We look at what you have shipped and how you reason about it

Integration and API engineering: secure service-to-service endpoints, third-party APIs, webhooks, and the patience to work with legacy banking systems that were not designed to be integrated

Security and auth judgment: OAuth and machine-to-machine auth, tenant-scoped access, secrets handling, no PII in logs. Our agents touch sensitive member data and operate under consumer-contact regulation

Customer presence: you can sit across from a VP of Collections, hear a request, and say "here is what I recommend and why", including when the answer is no. You are comfortable making calls in the room and owning them afterwards

Code-quality judgment under deadline pressure: you take on debt deliberately, name it, and pay it down, rather than gold-plating or leaving silent debt behind

Willingness to travel: roughly 20% on average, with one- to two-week stretches around kickoffs and go-lives. Based in the US, able to travel on short notice

Genuine appetite for LLM agents: eval discipline for non-deterministic systems, reading a system prompt like code, understanding that some decisions must never reach the model. Curiosity plus shipped work is enough; research depth is not required

Nice to have, explicitly not required: voice and telephony (LiveKit, Twilio), Temporal or event-driven orchestration, Python, core banking or LOS integration experience, credit union or banking domain knowledge

#340. Senior Legal Counsel, Data Privacy at Kit

Kit is the email marketing platform experts choose to grow their audience, deepen their relationships, and build a business around the work they love. For coaches, YouTubers, authors, podcasters, and other creatives, there isn't a better marketing hub to rely on to grow audiences, automate email marketing, and sell digital products — all within one platform.More importantly, there isn't a team more committed to helping creators earn a living. We're on a mission to help creators earn $1 billion using our creator marketing platform. We have always been 100% independent and 100% remote.We are proud to have built a product that our customers love, and we look for people who have enthusiasm and belief in our mission, vision, and values to join our team. We're also embracing AI thoughtfully — both in how we build and how we hire to ensure our team is adaptable, innovative, and ready for what's next.

You'll report to our Chief Operating Officer, Brian Bevel, and partner regularly with leaders across product, sales, finance, and people operations. You'll own our core legal work in-house, reduce the need for outside counsel, and know when specialized outside counsel is truly needed.

First year: Help Kit operate at a higher level of legal maturity across privacy, compliance, product counsel, commercial contracts, and security support. Establish durable systems that allow teams to answer common questions independently while escalating higher-risk matters appropriately. Help us treat privacy, data, and compliance as strategic enablers—not just boxes to check—and significantly reduce our reliance on outside counsel for work we can handle effectively in-house.

Deep expertise in data, compliance, and product—this is where you'll spend most of your time.

Strong ability to navigate U.S. and European data privacy laws (e.g., GDPR, CCPA), including familiarity with data controller vs. processor distinctions and how they shape vendor and product decisions.

Ability to translate privacy and compliance requirements into scalable playbooks, templates, intake processes, and self-service guidance

Experience supporting customer security questionnaires and partnering effectively with security, sales, product, and engineering teams

Familiarity with SOC 2 Type II and the legal, privacy, and customer requirements associated with it, even if you haven't directly owned a certification process

Understanding of intellectual property law, especially related to brand, content, and software

Understanding of commercial contracts—you'll become the go-to person for these at Kit.

Clear communicator and trusted advisor—able to simplify complexity and help others make informed decisions

Experience as in-house counsel at a tech company or serving a tech portfolio at a top-tier firm that's well-known for their work with startups (e.g., Fenwick & West, Cooley)

J.D. from an accredited law school in the United States

Active member in good standing of a State Bar Association

Strategic thinker who sees legal as a lever, not a blocker

Deeply curious and business-oriented—you start by understanding the goals, then explore the smartest paths to get there.

Collaborative partner who can navigate conflict productively

Deep belief that creator success is our success—you consider both Kit and our customers in every recommendation

A "how might we" problem-solver who finds creative, business-aligned paths through legal challenges

Needing a team of in-house peers or co-counsel to pressure-test every decision—you'll be our sole in-house legal expert, with outside counsel available as needed

A strongly risk-averse or "no-before-yes" mindset—we need you to help us move, not just stop us from tripping

Thinking in a legal vacuum—if you're not factoring in our goals, numbers, or creators, your advice won't land

Struggling with speed or ownership—if you prefer long timelines or wait to be told what to do, this won't be the right environment. We move quickly and expect people to take initiative, spot problems, and drive solutions.

We're 100% remote with team members across the globe. For this role, we're looking for someone located in the United States.

Kit has standardized salaries based on position, no matter where you live. This role is an individual contributor level 4 ($227,000) or 5 ($252,000). Our other perks and benefits include:

We cover up to $2,100 per month toward medical premiums, with dental and vision premiums fully covered. We offer Health Insurance plans through Aetna

$2,000 equipment allowance for your first two years, $1,000 budget every following two years. Company-provided laptops are issued to every Kit team member and are not included in the equipment budget

Individual learning + development budget ($3,500/year)

Childcare benefit up to $3,000 annually through JOON

Twenty (20) days of paid time off during each year of employment

Paid paid vacation: An after-tax bonus of $1,000 for taking five consecutive days of vacation where you’re fully unplugged from work

Two weeks of paid sick time each year, including mental health + well being days

Twelve (12) weeks paid parental leave and flexible scheduling in your child’s first year

Up to six weeks of paid bereavement leave, medical leave, and disaster after six months of employment, two weeks of each paid leave in your first six months

Winter Break Closure: Kit closes for a week at the end of December, giving everyone a collective break to enjoy the holiday season. Essential support services remain available, with teams coordinating to ensure coverage during this period

Four-week, paid sabbatical after five years with the team

Fantastic in-person or virtual retreats with the team twice a year

We usually receive a large number of applications, and our goal is to follow up with you within two weeks. You’ll hear from us either way. Here’s what you can expect from the rest of our hiring process:

A phone screen with our recruiter (30 min)

Panel interview with cross functional stakeholders (60 min)

We’ll keep you informed through every step. To get started, complete this application, including a cover letter and answers to the questions on the next page. We read every single application, and your cover letter and responses help put your experience into context.

We value diversity in all of its forms. Research tells us that applicants who are female or non-binary, as well as applicants who are people of color, are less likely to apply for roles they do not feel 100% qualified for. If you think you meet more than 50% of our requirements but fewer than 100% of them, please apply.

We’re imperfect communicators, so think of our job postings as the starting point for discussion rather than proof that you shouldn’t apply.

Partner with Product and Policy on mitigations that address root causes, not just individual cases

Working knowledge of marketing attribution and campaign measurement — UTM and event pipelines, cost-per-acquisition math, and the vendors who sell it

You've run a build/buy/partner evaluation and defended the recommendation

You communicate priorities, timelines, and tradeoffs to senior stakeholders plainly

Uses AI tooling natively as part of your product workflow

Looking to join a world-class blockchain development team? Ava Labs makes it simple to deploy high-performance solutions for Web3, led by innovations on Avalanche. Ava Labs is redefining the way people create value with Web3. Join us as we empower people to easily and freely digitize all the world’s assets on one open, programmable blockchain platform.

We're hiring a Staff Engineer for the Developer Infrastructure team within Platform Engineering at Ava Labs. Platform Engineering builds and operates the core of the Avalanche network: consensus engines, the P-Chain, virtual machines, and the systems that let many virtual machines interoperate as one network.

Your job is to make the teams building those systems faster and more confident in what they ship. You will work across Platform Engineering to understand where development is slow, fragile, hard to reason about, or insufficiently automated, then build durable infrastructure, tooling, shared knowledge, and technical processes that make better engineering outcomes easier and more repeatable.

The work will typically span CI/CD, ephemeral environments, automated end-to-end testing, chaos and resilience testing, observability, performance infrastructure, and developer workflows, but we are less interested in narrow domain ownership than in the desire and ability to reduce engineering friction and risk. This is a hands-on role: you will be in the code, not adjacent to it.

Partner with teams across Platform Engineering to understand how they build, test, release, observe, and debug, then identify what is worth fixing, and how. Illustrative examples:

Support and evolve our CI/CD pipeline, currently built on Bazel and GitHub Actions, into a fast and trustworthy signal of code quality across unit tests, end-to-end tests, performance tests, and other release-critical checks.

Make ephemeral and long-running test environments easier to provision, inspect, compare, and retire.

Evolve observability infrastructure to collect useful data from diverse environments and compare coherently across runs, versions, and configurations to reveal regressions and highlight improvements.

Improve confidence in the correctness and resilience of consensus, networking, and protocol-adjacent systems through end-to-end testing, fuzzing, chaos engineering, and failure-oriented test design.

Turn recurring team pain points into tools, automation and documentation, and spread the context — through design reviews, examples, and technical writing — so teams extend what you build without routing through you.

Do the unglamorous work visibly so others emulate you: debugging flaky tests, tightening release checks, improving documentation, reviewing tool adoption, and following through until a system is genuinely useful.

You are a self-starter with deep curiosity. You are comfortable diving into someone else’s code to understand how it works, and you treat the code as the source of truth.

You have strong engineering judgment, and an instinct for when code, tests, or systems are not maintainable, observable, or reproducible enough. You can explain the tradeoffs behind your calls.

You build cross-team agreement through working software and demonstrated judgment rather than process mandates. Teams trust you because your work makes their work better.

You care about reliability, and you are motivated by building the infrastructure that helps other engineers ship with confidence.

You find the boundaries between application and infrastructure, product code and developer tooling, more fluid than people pretend.

You listen carefully, yet you are still willing to prototype an idea before it is fully proven.

You can make a high bar feel practical. You push for better engineering outcomes in a way that makes people want to work with you, not around you.

You have operated at Staff scope before, regardless of title: you can point to a workstream you created or transformed, one that other teams came to depend on.

7+ years writing production software, with strong ability in Go and/or Rust.

Experience in large legacy codebases with multiple teams and shared ownership boundaries.

Experience building or significantly improving developer infrastructure, CI/CD, test infrastructure, observability, release tooling, or comparable engineering productivity systems.

Strong testing discipline, the ability to diagnose and pragmatically relieve bottlenecks.

Working fluency with Linux, containers, and infrastructure-as-code.

GitHub Actions or similar CI/CD systems; Bazel or similar build systems.

Distributed systems, blockchain infrastructure, consensus systems, P2P networking, or other high-reliability systems.

Kubernetes or similar orchestration frameworks.

Large-scale observability: tracing, profiling, metrics.

Using data to drive performance optimization.

Chaos engineering, fuzzing, property-based testing, and failure-injection systems.

You want to set technical direction without writing code.

You want to own a fixed infrastructure domain in isolation from the teams using it.

You prefer prescribing process over building tools and feedback loops that make better practices easier to follow.

You consider tests, documentation, migrations, debugging, and adoption work beneath Staff-level engineering.

You'll support product teams that ship features without dedicated QA. Your job is not to become their testing safety net. It's to build the tooling and practices that let builders own quality themselves — and to stay close enough to real features to know where that tooling breaks.

Camunda also ships AI capabilities in its own product, so the evaluation practice you build for agent-driven testing feeds directly into how we test non-deterministic features.

You'll join colleagues who live our FAITH values: Focus, Ambition, Integrity, Talent and Humor.

Curious about the kind of challenges you'll work on at Camunda? Watch this quick 30-minute talk from our engineers to learn more about the new Camunda Exporter and how we’re solving complex problems at scale

Build and operate agents across the testing lifecycle — test design, generation, maintenance, execution and failure triage.

Own the infrastructure that makes agent-driven testing reliable: environments, test data, tool interfaces, guardrails, runtime and cost control.

Define how we measure agent output quality, so teams can trust results instead of hand-reviewing them.

Apply that evaluation practice to testing Camunda 8's own AI capabilities.

Work hands-on with new features as teams build them, enough to keep the tooling honest.

Raise the quality capability of teams — patterns, tooling, enablement. Success is what builders can do themselves, not the number of tests you wrote.

Ability and/or willingness to use our product

5+ years as a software engineer. You write production code daily and would be credible on a product team; quality is your domain, not a step down from development.

Production experience building test infrastructure, developer tooling or internal platforms that other engineers depend on — designed and owned, not just extended.

Hands-on work with LLMs or agent frameworks: prompt and context design, tool use, handling non-determinism, and evaluating output quality. This is the differentiator for the role.

Comfort with distributed systems and CI at scale. Camunda 8 is a process orchestration platform; testing it means reasoning about concurrency, state and timing.

The ability to drive adoption in teams that don't report to you. You've built something another team chose to use, and you know what to do when the first version isn't picked up.

Experience evaluating or benchmarking LLM systems.

Java, TypeScript or Python; Kubernetes and Helm.

Background in developer tooling or platform engineering.

Run the vendor security review program, from intake to periodic re-review

Own the security questionnaire and trust center workflow

Embed compliance requirements into the SDLC and change management so they're enforced by tooling, not by reminders

Reduce the number of things a human has to do to pass an audit every quarter

We're hiring for Self-Managed Experience (SMX) — the team responsible for making Camunda 8 deployable in a self-service way for customers who run their own infrastructure. SMX covers two areas of work: installation artifacts (Helm chart, Docker Compose, C8Run) and reference architectures & cloud infrastructure (AWS, GCP, Azure).

This role sits primarily on the installation artifacts side — building, maintaining, and releasing the artifacts that ship Camunda 8 to every self-managed customer. You'll be fully embedded in that area day-to-day, but you'll work alongside the reference-architecture side of the team regularly, and SMX is actively working toward enabling every engineer to review and contribute across both stacks over time.

SMX is also shifting from a purely artifact- and ops-focused team toward one in which engineers bring customer judgment and product sense alongside technical depth. That means engaging directly with the teams closest to customers — Support, Consulting, Presales — and using that signal to help shape what we prioritize, not just executing a fully-specced ticket.

You'll find plenty of room to leave your own footprint: deployment automation, software and infrastructure testing, multi-region setups, and developer experience are all live areas of investment as the team matures from "basic install" toward full-lifecycle ownership (upgrades, backup/restore, disaster recovery).

Curious about the kind of challenges you'll work on at Camunda? Watch this quick 30-minute talk from our engineers to learn more about the new Camunda Exporter and how we’re solving complex problems at scale

Build, maintain, and release C8 distribution artifacts for self-managed customers — Helm Charts (Kubernetes), C8Run, and Docker Compose — along with their documentation.

Improve the reliability and usability of deployment artifacts across the full customer lifecycle: installation, upgrades, and day-2 operations, not just initial deployment.

Engage directly with internal customer-facing teams (Support, Consulting, Presales) to understand real deployment problems, and use that signal to help shape what gets prioritized — not just how it gets built. Collaborate with Development Teams, Product Management, QA, and Documentation to ship integrated, tested, and documented releases.

Take part in the team's shared medic rotation and resolve engineering-level support cases, feeding learnings back into development.

Contribute to the shared tooling (review, deployment, and test tooling) that SMX is building so other Camunda teams can adopt it — this is one of the team's current investment areas.

What success looks like (first ~3 months):

Taken on your first medic rotation slot and support tickets to understand the stack, customer challenges, and deployment environments.

Improved onboarding or documentation, turning your own ramp-up experience into concrete improvements.

Contributed to artifact fixes, CI/CD enhancements, or test automation that strengthens release quality.

Deliver structural improvement initiatives — a feature request, or a test/release improvement.

Built working relationships with engineering, QA, and product peers, and started building context on the reference-architecture side of the team.

Started forming your own view of a customer pain point from firsthand signal (support tickets, consulting feedback), not just from a ticket description.

Ability and/or willingness to use our product, with genuine curiosity about the customer problem behind a ticket — comfortable asking "should we build this" as well as "how do we build this."

Strong expertise in building, operating, and maintaining Helm Charts; deploying applications on Kubernetes; implementing CI/CD pipelines with GitHub Actions; and managing infrastructure as code (e.g., Terraform).

A pragmatic and autonomous approach to programming and problem-solving.

You thrive as a manager of one — you build it, you own it — and take pride in delivering maintainable, operable software.

#457. Organic Social Media Manager at Winona

Winona is one of the leading telemedicine companies providing HRT for women in menopause. We’ve built all of our technology in house including an EHR, patient care admin system, patient portal, website, marketing technology etc. Winona has two compounding pharmacies and a team of in house physicians providing world-class care via a fully vertically integrated business model.

The Organic Social Media Manager is responsible for the day-to-day operation of Winona's organic social channels: planning the content calendar, briefing the teams and creators who produce the work, publishing across platforms, and engaging externally to grow reach. The role translates the channel strategy set by the Head of Social and the performance insights provided by Growth into a consistent, on-brand presence that reaches women navigating menopause.

This is a planning and creative direction role. The Organic Social Media Manager owns the content plan and the posting strategy — what is produced, for which platform, when, and how often — and is expected to bring an independent point of view on the audience rather than executing recommendations without interpretation. Overarching channel strategy and all paid media remain outside the role.

Head of Social — channel strategy, priorities, quarterly goals, and final content approval

Growth — performance insights and content recommendations, including signals from Community and Lifecycle on messaging performance. These inform the content plan; they do not replace the Organic Social Media Manager's own assessment of the audience

Creative/Design — produces statics and video against briefs provided by this role

Content/SEO — supplies long-form editorial for adaptation to social

Patient Services — responds to inbound comments and direct messages regarding the brand, products, orders, and clinical questions. This role routes those inquiries and provides advance notice of launches, campaigns, and posts likely to generate volume

Community — owns the Winona community app and platform. Insight is shared in both directions and cross-promotion is coordinated where appropriate

Paid — owns the influencer program and supplies this role with trending TikTok content produced by creators for organic use. This role may recommend creators and repurpose approved creator content, but does not brief, negotiate, or manage paid partnerships

PR (under Community) — amplification opportunities, press coverage, and any situation requiring a coordinated response

Copy — edits captions drafted by this role. Caption strategy and first drafts belong to Social; Copy provides an editorial pass for clarity, accuracy, and brand consistency

Paid social strategy, buying, and budget management

The influencer program, including briefs, contracts, and paid creator relationships

Responding to inbound questions in comments and direct messages

Posting strategy, content planning, and publishing

Own the posting strategy across all owned channels: cadence, frequency, timing, sequencing, and platform-specific publishing conventions. The posting strategy is set by this role, informed by performance data and operating within the channel strategy and goals established by the Head of Social.

Build and maintain the rolling content calendar, determining content mix and formats, and execute all publishing. Ensure live content remains accurate and current; when a product detail, price, or claim changes, identify and correct affected posts.

Publish and maintain organic content for Winona's brand persona accounts, in addition to the primary Winona accounts. Each persona carries a distinct voice, audience, and content remit, and must remain consistent over time and clearly differentiated from the main brand account and from one another.

This includes planning each persona's content, originating or adapting material suited to that persona, and publishing on its own cadence.

Develop concepts and create the ClickUp tickets that direct all production. Each ticket must contain quality guidelines sufficient for the creative teams to build the intended asset without further direction: concept, hook, script or talking points, format and specifications, reference material, and the outcome the content is meant to achieve.

Ticket quality is the central competency of this role. An effective ticket is specific enough for the creative teams to execute without follow-up, while leaving creators sufficient latitude to retain an authentic voice. Imprecise tickets consume Creative capacity and are a common cause of production delays and rework.

Repurposing content from paid media and other channels

Identify and adapt content originally produced for paid media, ambassador programs, and other channels for use on organic social. Review incoming creative and the ClickUp submission queue, assessing each asset against the standards of the platform it would run on.

Much of the paid library is already social-native: creator clips and short-form video built for feed. The work is therefore less about screening out unusable assets than about selecting what merits an organic placement, reworking hooks and captions for an audience that has not opted into an advertisement, and pacing usage so the channel does not read as recycled advertising.

Own caption strategy and produce the first drafts of all hooks and captions, using AI tools to generate and refine options. Drafts are submitted to Copy for an editorial pass. Accountability for whether a caption reads as native to the platform and appropriate to its placement rests with this role.

Engage proactively on external accounts — creators, practitioners, menopause advocates, adjacent brands, and the conversations the target audience is already having — to build reach, relationships, and recognition for Winona. This is a defined deliverable rather than discretionary work, and it is distinct from inbox management.

Engagement should be substantive and add value to the conversation. It excludes responding to critics, participating in competitor comment sections, and answering clinical or product questions in third-party threads. Relationships that progress toward a paid partnership are handed to the Paid team.

Inbound comments and direct messages to Winona's own accounts are answered by Patient Services. This role routes them and escalates any reputationally sensitive matter to the Head of Social immediately.

Deliver regular performance reporting against the KPIs set by the Head of Social, covering results, the factors that drove them, and recommended next tests. Escalate anomalous performance as it is identified rather than holding it for the monthly report.

3–5 years managing organic social for a brand or agency, with a body of work the candidate can present and explain the reasoning behind.

Demonstrated strength in creative briefing: the ability to translate an idea into a production ticket the creative teams can execute correctly the first time, including concept, hook, script, format specifications, and reference material.

A strong editorial eye for short-form video. The role does not require shooting or editing, but does require the judgment to direct others effectively.

Strong copywriting, particularly hooks, captions, and conversational engagement.

Practical fluency with AI writing tools and the editorial judgment to distinguish usable output from generic output.

Thorough working knowledge of Instagram and TikTok mechanics, including formats, audio, algorithm behavior, and current performance trends.

Daily, short-form-first presence on our primary channels: Instagram, TikTok, and Facebook.

Consistent cadence on secondary channels: YouTube Shorts, X, and Pinterest.

A distinct, more corporate register for LinkedIn, and substantive, disclosed long-form answers on Quora.

Disciplined listening-only monitoring on Reddit — no posting there without explicit sign-off.

Strong analytical skills: the ability to interpret performance reporting and form a defensible point of view from it.

Proven reliability in a role with a fixed publishing schedule and a live audience

The range to write and publish in multiple distinct voices, maintaining separate persona accounts without them converging on a single tone.

Experience in healthcare, telehealth, supplements, or wellness.

A record of account growth driven by outbound engagement and creator relationships, not publishing alone.

Familiarity with menopause, perimenopause, or women's midlife health, whether professional, academic, or personal.

Substantive empathy for women in their 40s and 50s whose health concerns have been dismissed, and the judgment to distinguish content that engages the audience from content that engages at their expense. Trends should be adapted to suit this audience rather than adopted wholesale.

Paid non-working holidays per country of residence

Medical/ Dental/ Vision insurance (US-W2)

Employee engagement activities and virtual gatherings

In line with our FAITH values (Focus, Ambition, Integrity, Talent, Humor), you’ll combine clear thinking, honest partnership, and a bias for action to drive long-term success for our customers and for Camunda.

Own a portfolio of enterprise customers and act as their primary strategic partner from onboarding through renewal—aligning on goals, success measures, and an adoption roadmap that delivers real business value.

Drive retention and expansion by managing health, risk, and opportunities across your accounts, partnering with Sales and internal teams to secure renewals and uncover meaningful growth opportunities.

Lead structured customer conversations (e.g., onboarding sessions, success plan reviews, value and health check-ins) that connect Camunda capabilities to customer outcomes in clear, business-friendly terms.

Use data to tell the story—leveraging usage, value, and health signals to prioritize actions, forecast outcomes, and make informed recommendations for both customers and internal stakeholders.

Project manage cross-functional work (with TAMs, Consulting, Product, and Support) to unblock customers, close the loop on issues, and keep complex programs moving forward.

Contribute to our Customer Success practice by sharing learnings, mentoring peers, and helping refine playbooks, processes, and tooling as our team and portfolio scale.

Ability and/or willingness to use our product.

Relevant experience: 6+ years in Customer Success, Strategic Account Management, or customer-facing consulting in B2B software, ideally working with enterprise customers.

Relationship & stakeholder management: Proven ability to build trust with senior and operational stakeholders, navigate complex organizations, and lead candid, outcome-focused conversations.

Commercial awareness & forecasting: Experience supporting or owning renewals and expansion in a recurring revenue model, including comfort with forecasting, pipeline hygiene, and risk/opportunity assessment.

Data-informed decision-making: Ability to interpret customer data (adoption, health signals, value metrics) and turn it into clear insights, priorities, and next steps for both customers and internal teams.

Communication & facilitation: Strong written and verbal communication skills, including leading customer meetings, presenting recommendations, and aligning cross-functional collaborators in a remote-first environment.

Experience working with customers in financial services, banking, insurance, or other regulated industries.

Experience with orchestration, automation, or adjacent domains (e.g., process improvement, workflow, integration platforms) and/or technical products.

Hands-on familiarity with Salesforce, Gainsight, or similar CRM/CS platforms for managing accounts, activities, and health.

Experience working closely with technical counterparts (e.g., Solution Architects, TAMs, Engineering, or Product) to drive adoption and resolve complex issues.

A track record of mentoring peers, contributing to playbooks, or helping shape how a Customer Success team operates.

#470. Engineering Manager - App Stores at Canonical

Canonical is a leading provider of open source software and operating systems to the global enterprise and technology markets. Our platform, Ubuntu, is very widely used in breakthrough enterprise initiatives such as public cloud, data science, AI, engineering innovation, and IoT. Our customers include the world's leading public cloud and silicon providers, and industry leaders in many sectors. The company is a pioneer of global distributed collaboration, with 1200+ colleagues in 75+ countries and very few office-based roles. Teams meet two to four times yearly in person, in interesting locations around the world, to align on strategy and execution.

The company is founder-led, profitable, and growing.

This is a technical management role to lead a team that develops Python and Golang micro-services that power our global software distribution engine. The world sees it as the Snap Store and Charmhub.io marketplaces, behind the scenes it is a unified system that understands key concepts in software distribution - architectures, releases, betas, release candidates, stable releases, branches and more. We are on a journey to transform the experience that people all over the world have with their open source software by significantly expanding the range of software we can deliver through this system. If you have a passion for clean APIs, believe that great engineers ship software calmly and regularly against an agile plan, and know that tests are the key to higher velocity and reliability, you'll fit right in.

This is a great opportunity to take part in engineering a highly scalable SaaS product (think about the load on our systems when one of our largest Ubuntu Desktop snaps is updated by the publisher, for instance). In addition, you will have the opportunity to learn from Canonical's world-class security team as we work collectively to deliver this capability, safely, to our customers around the world.

As an Engineering Manager at Canonical, you must be technically strong, but your main responsibility is to run an effective team and develop the colleagues you manage. You will develop and review code as a leader, but know that the best way to improve the product is to ensure that the whole team is focused, productive and unblocked. You are expected to help them grow as engineers, do meaningful work, do it outstandingly well, find professional and personal satisfaction, and work well with colleagues and the community. You will also be expected to be a positive influence on culture, facilitate technical delivery, and regularly reflect with your team on strategy and execution. You will collaborate closely with other Engineering Managers, product managers, and architects, producing an engineering roadmap with ambitious and achievable goals.

We expect Engineering Managers to be fluent in the programming language, architecture, and components that their team uses. Code reviews and architectural leadership are part of the job. The commitment to healthy engineering practices, documentation, quality and performance optimisation is as important, as is the requirement for fair and clear management, and the obligation to ensure a high-performing team.

This is a great opportunity to really learn how to do engineering of a highly-scalable SaaS product (think about the load on our systems when one of our largest Ubuntu Desktop snaps is updated by the publisher, for instance).  In addition, you will have the opportunity to learn from Canonical's world-class security team as we work collectively to deliver this capability, safely, to our customers around the world.

Location: This role may be based remotely in the Americas, Europe, Middle East or Africa time zones.

Your base pay will depend on various factors including your geographical location, level of experience, knowledge and skills. In addition to the benefits above, certain roles are also eligible for additional benefits and rewards including annual bonuses and sales incentives based on revenue or utilisation. Our compensation philosophy is to ensure equity right across our global workforce.

In addition to a competitive base pay, we provide all team members with additional benefits, which reflect our values and ideals. Please note that additional benefits may apply depending on the work location and, for more information on these, you can ask in the later stages of the recruitment process.

Canonical is a pioneering tech firm at the forefront of the global move to open source. As the company that publishes Ubuntu, one of the most important open-source projects and the platform for AI, IoT, and the cloud, we are changing the world of software. We recruit on a global basis and set a very high standard for people joining the company. We expect excellence; in order to succeed, we need to be the best at what we do. Most colleagues at Canonical have worked from home since our inception in 2004.​ Working here is a step into the future and will challenge you to think differently, work smarter, learn new skills, and raise your game.

We are proud to foster a workplace free from discrimination. Diversity of experience, perspectives, and background create a better work environment and better products.Whatever your identity, we will give your application fair consideration.

Build features for teams, organizations, and developer communities

Help review and shape code from peers to ensure quality, security, and best practices

#473. Senior Site Reliability Engineer at Camunda

Camunda is the enterprise platform for agentic orchestration, enabling organizations to coordinate AI agents, people, and systems across complex, end-to-end business processes. With built-in governance, auditability, and human oversight, Camunda gives enterprises the control they need to move AI from pilots to production — safely and at scale. Trusted by over 700 organizations worldwide, including 9 of top 10 US banks, Camunda helps enterprises boost operational efficiency, accelerate time-to-value, and deliver better customer experiences.Fully remote and global, we are in the middle of something bigger: transforming into an AI-first organisation, built on our own platform. We use Agentic AI to automate, orchestrate intelligent processes, and elevate human contribution across every team.Named GP Bullhound’s Top 100 Next Unicorn list, 2025 Great Place to Work certified. Visionary in 2025 Gartner® Magic Quadrant™ for Business Orchestration and Automation Technologies. ranked 3rd in Flexa's 2026 Most Flexible Companies, We’re growing fast and looking for top talent to join our team. If you want meaningful work, visible impact and put something genuinely rare on your CV, keep reading.

We're looking for a Senior Site Reliability Engineer who's passionate about building reliable, scalable infrastructure that helps developers ship better software faster. You'll design and maintain our Kubernetes-based multi-cloud platform, improve our monitoring and observability tools, and collaborate with product and engineering teams to solve real problems in real time. This is a role where you'll own the systems that power Camunda, drive automation that raises the bar for everyone, and mentor others who want to do the same. If you thrive on building things that work well and don't break when they shouldn't, we'd love to talk.

Design and maintain our infrastructure – You'll evolve our Kubernetes-based, multi-cloud platform architecture, ensuring it's available, scalable, and fault-tolerant. You'll establish configuration best practices and network services that our teams rely on.

Build observability that matters – Implement and improve monitoring and alerting tools that give both SREs and developers real visibility into system health and performance. Make it easy for teams to understand what's happening across our stack.

Own your systems end-to-end – You'll adopt a "you build it, you run it" mentality, which means participating in on-call rotations and being the go-to person when things need quick fixes. You'll create runbooks and automation that turn complex problems into manageable processes.

Ship features and improvements with product teams – Work cross-functionally with product engineering, product management, and support to define and deliver features that move the needle. Bring your expertise to the table early and often.

Push automation to the next level – Identify repetitive work and automate it away. Share what you learn with your teammates so everyone gets better at their craft. We measure progress by the quality of our systems, not hours worked.

Be the expert others learn from – Help less experienced engineers tackle complex infrastructure challenges. Break down technical problems into clear steps and support others in growing their skills.

Deep hands-on experience with Kubernetes – You've built, deployed, and maintained Kubernetes clusters in production environments. You understand how to manage workloads, networking, and storage at scale.

Infrastructure as code expertise – You're fluent in tools like Terraform (or similar IaC tools) and know how to version, test, and safely deploy infrastructure changes.

Demonstrated experience in monitoring and observability – You've worked with tools like Prometheus, Grafana, or similar platforms to instrument systems and alert on what matters.

Strong 3rd-level support and incident response skills – You've responded to production incidents, diagnosed complex issues, and communicated clearly with stakeholders under pressure. You understand root cause analysis and how to prevent issues from happening again.

A passion for automation and raising the quality bar – You see manual work as a problem to be solved. You care deeply about building systems that are reliable, maintainable, and easy to understand.

Responsible use of AI tools – You leverage AI for research, code review, documentation, test generation, and automation to improve your effectiveness. You know how to validate AI outputs against requirements, never share confidential or personal data with AI systems without authorization, and always retain human accountability for decisions and deliverables.

Experience with major cloud providers – You've worked with AWS (EKS), Google Cloud Platform (GKE), or similar managed Kubernetes services.

ArgoCD or GitOps workflows – You've used declarative, Git-driven infrastructure management to keep systems in sync.

Proficiency in Python, Go, or similar languages – You write scripts and automation tools that solve real problems.

Experience with SLOs and alerting frameworks – You've helped teams define meaningful service level objectives and set up alerts that don't cry wolf.

#474. Director of Revenue Operations at Uscreen

At Uscreen, we help creators build something that lasts, powering independent video businesses to build sustainable revenue and scale their impact. We're a fast-growing SaaS company, and our all-in-one video membership platform helps creators generate revenue through subscriptions, communities, courses, and live-streamed events across web, mobile, and TV apps.

We're hiring a Director of Revenue Operations to own the systems, data, and strategy that drive revenue performance across Sales, Marketing, and Customer Success. This is the person who connects the dots: how we map and segment our market, how leads are scored and routed, how reps are territoried and incentivized, how pipeline is forecast, and how all of that flows between the CRM, the warehouse, and the teams who act on it.

This is a build role. The foundations are here: a CRM with real history in it, a data warehouse that holds our source of truth, an outbound motion getting off the ground, and a sales team with momentum. What's missing is someone to connect them into one engine and own what comes out of it. You'll get real latitude to decide how this function works, and you'll be expected to build it yourself rather than direct it from a distance.

You'll do it inside an AI-native team. We treat AI as a core part of how we work, and in this role especially: mapping and enriching a market that no off-the-shelf database covers well, automating the operational work that shouldn't take a human, and getting to answers faster than a traditional ops function could.

Strategic Projects & Cross-Functional Support

#476. Customer Growth Specialist at Uscreen

Uscreen is the video monetization platform for businesses building recurring revenue from video content. Our customers replace a patchwork stack of separate hosting, community, courses, email, and app vendors with one branded experience across web, mobile, and TV.

The platform is only half of it. We believe growth requires behavior, not just software. Customers don't stall because a feature is missing. They stall because they priced wrong, never built an email list, or launched an offer nobody wanted. Coaching is how we fix that, and it's part of the product rather than an add-on.

We have a cohort of smaller video businesses where retention is not where it should be. Nobody owns it today. You will. That means the revenue that stays in that segment, and the revenue that grows inside it, is yours. Your lemonade stand, your numbers, your call on how to run it.

This is a coaching role measured in dollars. You'll be accountable for gross revenue retention in your cohort first, and expansion second. Not tickets closed, not calls booked.

It's also a one-to-many job. Your cohort is larger than a 1:1 book, so the work is designing coaching that scales: cohort programs, group sessions, office hours, triggered outreach when the data says a business is drifting. You'll build that motion rather than inherit it.

Someone who has grown something online and can explain how. Maybe you ran marketing for a small business, coached founders, built your own audience, or worked inside a membership or subscription business. What matters is that you can sit with an operator, see the real constraint, and say the honest thing.

#481. Customer Growth Specialist at Uscreen

Uscreen is the video monetization platform for businesses building recurring revenue from video content. Our customers replace a patchwork stack of separate hosting, community, courses, email, and app vendors with one branded experience across web, mobile, and TV.

The platform is only half of it. We believe growth requires behavior, not just software. Customers don't stall because a feature is missing. They stall because they priced wrong, never built an email list, or launched an offer nobody wanted. Coaching is how we fix that, and it's part of the product rather than an add-on.

We have a cohort of smaller video businesses where retention is not where it should be. Nobody owns it today. You will. That means the revenue that stays in that segment, and the revenue that grows inside it, is yours. Your lemonade stand, your numbers, your call on how to run it.

This is a coaching role measured in dollars. You'll be accountable for gross revenue retention in your cohort first, and expansion second. Not tickets closed, not calls booked.

It's also a one-to-many job. Your cohort is larger than a 1:1 book, so the work is designing coaching that scales: cohort programs, group sessions, office hours, triggered outreach when the data says a business is drifting. You'll build that motion rather than inherit it.

Someone who has grown something online and can explain how. Maybe you ran marketing for a small business, coached founders, built your own audience, or worked inside a membership or subscription business. What matters is that you can sit with an operator, see the real constraint, and say the honest thing.
